plain: A conference on gravity at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is said to have set off a burst of research into anti-gravity in the 1950s. A researcher named Eric Weinstein calls it famous and says it "kicks a lot of this off," and Michels returns to it across many episodes, mostly dating it to 1957 (once to 1956), saying it was hosted by a man named Agnew Bahnson and brought together top physicists such as John Wheeler, Richard Feynman and Freeman Dyson, along with Louis Witten from the Martin company. Michels also says it was sponsored by Wright Air Field, which became Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, a place he calls "perhaps the epicenter of all UFO mythology," and ties the meeting to the birth of quantum gravity and string theory. A guest named Bob Maguire credits Wheeler with starting it, backed by two industrialists, with Feynman as first speaker. To the tellers, it suggests serious science and military interest in controlling gravity began there.
